sources.title: The Sleeping Agent: What Gist-Based Context Compression Loses and Why
sources.summary: Gist-based context compression---summarising older conversation history into compact representations---is a common approach in long-horizon language model agents, yet its effect on different types of memory retrieval is poorly understood. We use Salience-Weighted Consolidation (SWC), a biologically-inspired compression framework motivated by sleep-based memory consolidation, as a diagnostic probe to study when gist compression helps and when it hurts. sources.title: Ontology-Grounded Project Memory for Coding Agents
sources.summary: Coding agents have become the primary means of generating new code in many software projects, and the resulting velocity of changes makes keeping track of the reasons behind those changes challenging. This paper introduces MOOSEDev, a system designed to give coding agents structured, ontology-grounded project memory. sources.title: SuperLocalMemory 4.0: The Governed Memory Operating System for AI Agents
sources.summary: We present SuperLocalMemory 4.0, a governed, local-first memory operating system for AI agents, unifying multi-channel retrieval under reciprocal-rank fusion, bi-temporal recall, multi-scope isolation, role-based access, verified erasure, and a hash-chained audit trail. sources.title: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked: Budgeted Verification Failures in Inherited Agent Memory
sources.summary: An agent that inherits a consolidated memory may inherit a constraint that was true when written and has since been withdrawn by a newer authoritative record. sources.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
sources.summary: Continually improving agents require dynamic interaction feedback beyond static supervision, yet direct real-environment interaction is costly, slow, unsafe, and hard to parallelize. World modeling offers a natural intermediate proxy that allows agents to query lower-cost, more controllable feedback before committing to real actions.
